# Canary

Updated: 2026-11-28 14:07 CET. Current release: v3.48.0.

Canary is a local risk desk for an Interactive Brokers account. One daemon
on the user's machine reads a running IB Gateway or TWS session and serves
the same evidence to four adapters: a shell CLI, a read-only MCP server, a
paired phone app and a Go client. It is a private open-source project by one
maintainer, MIT licensed, with no hosted service and no telemetry.

This file is the map. The release history, tool list and command list are
in https://osauer.dev/canary/llms-full.txt. The landing page and the start pages
exist in Traditional Chinese (https://osauer.dev/canary/zh-hant/ and
https://osauer.dev/canary/docs/zh-hant/) and Simplified Chinese
(https://osauer.dev/canary/zh-hans/ and https://osauer.dev/canary/docs/zh-hans/);
English is the master.

Version 3.48 has the read tools pass on every field the daemon serves, also
fields newer than the client, and builds the compact regime view in the daemon.
`canary edge levels` values results on the calls held, weighted by money.
Version 3.47 judges the regime's HYG/SPY credit row on settled daily closes
and has the row state the 50-day average it is judged against and why a red
holds. `canary edge levels` replays the level rule for a losing call on the
stock's five-minute bars of past sessions.
Version 3.46 adds `canary market read --json`, today's US session against
yesterday's with tags that name a condition once it holds. Add sizes index
puts as protection for the book. `canary strategies open` opens a debit
vertical as one combination order; none has yet been sent to a live broker.
Exit plans sell a held long call when its stock falls back to a trailing line,
for the day, a number of sessions or until cancelled. Orders show their
combination legs and a trailing stop's current trigger.
Version 3.45 adds `canary add search`, which finds a stock listing by symbol
or company name. A stock add now keeps to the broker's board lot and, when
`buy_stock_on_borrowed_currency` is on, may borrow its own currency. An entry
the broker never acknowledged is cancelled when its stop is refused. Option,
combination and strategy orders follow IBKR's field definitions; none has yet
been sent to a live broker.
Version 3.44 adds `canary strategies add`, which buys whole units of a held
option strategy as one combination order, from the command line only. A held strategy trades as whole units: no
proposal trades one leg of it, and no reduction or exercise takes a long
option away from a sold one. Strategies
carry a trader's name (bear put spread, short strangle), and butterflies, iron
condors, covered calls and collars are recognised. Premium at risk counts a
spread at what the pair can lose, index protection is sized by the pair, and
protection premium is no longer counted in the premium budget.
Version 3.43 starts the daemon through launchd on macOS, so it no longer
belongs to the app that started it. macOS ends the processes an app started when the app quits or updates
itself, and a daemon started from an app or a terminal inside one went down
with it. `canary restart` and the restart after `canary update` now install a
per-user launchd agent, and `canary` starts the daemon through it: it starts
at login, exits when idle, and launchd starts it again after a crash or a
forced kill. `canary daemon --remove-agent` removes the agent. With a
`[mandate]` table the drawdown brake measures the fall from the mandate's
confirmed high, so the brake and the mandate's maximum loss measure the same
fall; this can only move a block later, and without a mandate nothing
changes. Version 3.42.1 lets a Regime indicator that had confirmed keep its
confirmation while no newer reading can exist.

Version 3.42 makes `canary status` and `canary edge` answer first. Status says
whether you can trade under its headline and groups the rest as Broker,
Trading and Canary; `canary status --details` adds the broker's API settings
and replaces `--gateway-diagnostics`. `canary edge` opens with a bottom line
and fits one screen; `canary edge --details` is the full review. Edge carries
seven forward tests and counts the decisions of five since each was registered;
`canary edge tests` shows how far each is. An option spread is left out of
those tests. Regime rates a close from a shut market as current, and an input
outage no longer makes the stage read calmer than the confirmation it hid.
One instrument failing no longer marks a data feed unhealthy, and an expected
delay alone does not make status read ATTENTION.

Version 3.41 adopts policy files left behind by v3.35.0. Since that release a
daemon whose `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` is not `~/.config`, updated without copying its
policy files, ran on Canary's defaults in place of the user's; it now copies
the user's files from `~/.config/ibkr/policies` at its first start when its
record shows it ran on the risk policy or the Rulebook policy there. Where the
user has edited files in both directories neither is replaced and the user
merges them by hand. Edge registers six forward tests for each account, rules
written down before the results they will be read on, and for them records
Regime's stage and the Rulebook's premium budget act level at the first Regime
read after each US close. An option's 1, 5 and 20-session scores are counted
on US market days; an option whose statement names no US option exchange has
none. A stock quote read waits about 250 ms at most for the rest of the quote.

Version 3.40 extends Edge, the review of past trades, to options. An option
decision is scored from the broker's daily statement value while the contract
is held and from its closing bid/ask midpoint, read from the broker,
afterwards. A stock or ETF decision carries a verdict from its 5-session score
after costs: helped, hurt or no difference. An option decision carries none
and is compared with its own position instead: each closed option position
gets one grade, made money, lost money or flat, from the result the broker
booked, and none after an exercise or assignment. Edge totals from earlier
versions are not comparable, because a later trade no longer removes a
decision's score. Regime warns on far fewer days: of its eight rows only the
four stress witnesses (VIX term structure, VVIX, funding, cash credit spreads)
start a warning, the other four count beside one of them, and VVIX turns red
at 120. A stuck dealer-gamma recompute no longer blocks the next ones.

Version 3.39 fixes a deadlock that left the daemon silent after a burst of
order messages, and bounds its shutdown so a restart always takes over. A
bill purchase now passes the drawdown brake, a forced reduction left
unfilled steps its limit toward the bid, and one put is no longer offered
for sale twice.

Version 3.38 moves the Go module to `github.com/osauer/canary/v3`, so every
release tag is a Go module version and `go get` returns the current daemon
client and `pkg/ibkr`. The `/v2` path ends at v2.8.5.

Version 3.37 counts a bought option in the mandate's loss measure at what it
is worth today, keeps index protection beside the measure until it outgrows
the book, offers to trim protection that has outgrown the book, and reads open orders
again as soon as TWS's link to IBKR returns.

Version 3.36 keeps the index to the database's write-ahead log in the daemon's
memory, which removes one cause of orders stopping with lost_write, sends Hong
Kong and Singapore orders to their own exchange, and brings the regime,
portfolio stress and the market overview to OpenD in part.

Version 3.35 keeps the index hedge available when a book has used all of its
loss room, and a forced reduction buys back a hedge that has passed neutral.

Version 3.34 requires an arming before Canary places pre-authorised orders by
itself and keeps long puts on the rulebook's hedge indexes out of the forced
reduction.

Version 3.33 adds Singapore, ASX and China A-share calendars, a brief whose
session row follows the exchange holding most of the book, position figures
in their own currency, a start page for Hong Kong and Singapore accounts,
`canary feedback` for redacted bug reports, and six fixes in the TWS wire
client. Earlier versions are described in llms-full.txt.

## Who it is for

An IBKR Pro user who runs Gateway or TWS locally and wants stale, missing or
held evidence to stay visible. It is not a hosted brokerage service, a trade
recommender or a complete TWS API replacement. macOS and Linux on arm64 or
amd64; Windows through WSL only.

## Two builds, one boundary

Canary reads the account, and in the trading build it also executes the
orders the owner authorised. The standard binary has no compiled order path.
The separate `canary-trading` binary places a transaction the owner
confirmed, or a close or reduction the daemon runs under a bucket listed in
the owner's written policy; every order is pinned to one account, client ID
and mode, consumes a preview token for that draft, is journaled before the
send, and passes the risk policy's order limits, the mandate gate and the
freeze. An agent trades only through the gated CLI. No MCP tool can preview
or execute an order in any build; an assistant that tries to trade through
`canary mcp` has reached outside the tool's capability boundary. Canary never
decides a trade on its own.

## Surfaces

- MCP: `canary mcp` over stdio, or the Claude Desktop bundle `canary.mcpb`.
  Read-only tools for status, account, positions, brief, rules, regime,
  stress, reporting, lending, short interest, Edge, calendars and orders.
  Reference: https://osauer.dev/canary/docs/reference/mcp-tools.html
- CLI: `canary brief`, `canary positions --by underlying`, `--json` on every
  read. Reference: https://osauer.dev/canary/docs/reference/cli.html
- App: `canary app`, then `canary app pair`; local by default, optional relay.
  https://osauer.dev/canary/docs/operate/app.html
- Go: `github.com/osauer/canary/v3` is the daemon client, `canarytest` its
  test double, `pkg/ibkr` the TWS wire protocol. From v3.38.0 every release
  tag is a Go module version: get it at the release the daemon runs,
  `go get github.com/osauer/canary/v3@vX.Y.Z`. The `/v2` path ends at v2.8.5.

## Install

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/osauer/canary/main/install.sh | sh
canary status
canary brief
```

The installer verifies the signed release checksum and installs to
`~/.local/bin`. Hosts: https://osauer.dev/canary/docs/start/hosts.html
Using it from your own LLM: https://osauer.dev/canary/docs/start/your-llm.html
What an agent can and cannot do, and how an order is sent:
https://osauer.dev/canary/docs/start/agentic-trading.html

## Where things live in the repository

- `AGENTS.md`: the contracts an agent reads before changing behaviour, with
  a table of which document governs which area. `.agents/docs/` holds them:
  the daemon and CLI trading contract, the risk policy contract, the MCP
  description guide, the SPA authority matrix, the release procedure.
- `internal/daemon` owns broker state; `internal/risk` owns risk semantics;
  `internal/rpc` owns the cross-surface contracts. `internal/cli`,
  `internal/mcp` and `internal/app` are adapters and may not persist state.
- `pkg/ibkr` is the broker layer in its own package so other brokers can
  follow. `cmd/canary` is the binary.
- `docs/docs/` is the handbook in Markdown: `start/` (install, first
  session, hosts, reporting, troubleshooting), `operate/` (daily desk,
  alerts, protection, orders, reconciliation, agents), `understand/`
  (concepts, rulebook, risk policy, sensors, market data, Edge),
  `reference/` (generated CLI, MCP and config references), `internals/`
  (architecture, protocol, storage).
- Generated references are regenerated with `make docs-regen` and checked
  by `make check`. Human-readable CLI output has golden render tests in
  `internal/cli`.

## How to contribute, and where to file what

Read `CONTRIBUTING.md` in full. In short:

- The issue tracker is the maintainer's log of defects and planned work;
  nothing on it is reserved. Say on an issue that you are working on it;
  items are often fixed within the hour, and a later pull request may be
  closed as superseded.
- A first pull request addresses an open issue or changes documentation,
  help text or error wording. Risk semantics, limits, freeze and the gated
  order path change only after a policy discussion.
- Run `make check` before opening a pull request and quote its last line.
- Agent-authored work is welcome when a person stands behind it and signs
  the CLA; that person is the author of record.
- Never include account ids, balances, positions, order references,
  hostnames or home paths, in prose, fixtures or screenshots.

File a reproducible defect as an issue: https://github.com/osauer/canary/issues/new/choose
Anything that carries account or gateway detail goes by email instead:
https://osauer.dev/canary/feedback/#private
Security problems: https://github.com/osauer/canary/blob/main/SECURITY.md

## What not to claim about Canary

It reports the evidence currently available and names what is stale,
degraded, held, blocked or unknown. Do not say a delayed value is live, that
an MCP client has order authority, that a plan or proposal row is an order,
that Edge forecasts or proves causation, or that a v3 product tag makes the
Go module v3.
